title: Treasury coupon announcement (3-Year new issue + 10-Year and 30-Year reopenings + 6/13/26-week bills) — the session that turns the January mid-quarter block from tentative into scheduled
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes, PDF CreationDate D:20260804173209-04'00'), FlateDecode streams inflated per page and rows rebuilt from Tm coordinates. SIX securities on page 3 carry the announcement date `Thursday, January 07, 2027`, read verbatim: `13-Week  BILL` and `26-Week  BILL` (both auction Monday, January 11, settle Thursday, January 14), `6-Week  BILL` (auction Tuesday, January 12, settle Thursday, January 14), `3-Year  NOTE` with NO `R` (auction Monday, January 11, settle Friday, January 15), `10-Year  NOTE / R` (auction Tuesday, January 12, settle Friday, January 15) and `30-Year  BOND / R` (auction Wednesday, January 13, settle Friday, January 15). The PDF's own legend reads `R --denotes reopening`. The ~11:00 a.m. ET announcement slot is standing convention inherited from the sibling coupon-announcement ledgers and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the announcement itself. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of treasury-30y-bond-2027-01-13, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED, NOT CANONICAL. Filed because it is the CONFIRMING PRIMARY for the event that proposed it: `treasury-30y-bond-2027-01-13` is `estimate` precisely until this announcement publishes, and the same is true of `treasury-10y-note-2027-01-12` (already proposed by the December 10-Year lane) and `treasury-3y-note-2027-01-11` (proposed in this same PR). The calendar tracks `treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-14` and `-2027-01-21` as first-class medium entries and has no `-2027-01-07`, so the block's own announcement was the one leg of the January mid-quarter cycle nobody owned. WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT DECIDE, stated so a later session does not over-read it: the coupon SIZES are not decided here. Treasury's quarterly refunding statement fixes nominal coupon sizes for its whole quarter, and the November-2026-to-January-2027 quarter was set at the 2026-11-04 refunding — already tracked as `treasury-refunding-2026-11-04`. This announcement PUBLISHES them, 64 days later. The nulls a reader should hold going in, all from `api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov` auctions_query pulled 2026-09-09: 3-Year NEW issue $58B (flat for 16 consecutive months, 2025-06-10 through 2026-09-08; the January prints were $40B in 2023, $52B in 2024, $58B in 2025 and 2026), 10-Year reopening and 30-Year reopening on their own grids — the 30-Year reopening null is $22B, 20 consecutive completed reopenings 2024-03-13 through 2026-07-09, and the separate 30-Year new-issue grid is $25B and must not be read across. The BILL sizes are the genuinely open numbers and January is where they historically move; this proposal makes no claim about them. WHAT IS ALSO PUBLISHED HERE and is not a size: the reopened CUSIPs. The 30-Year leg reopens the bond the 2026-11-12 new issue creates, and the 10-Year leg the note the 2026-11-10 new issue creates — neither security exists today, so no CUSIP is predicted. Reading it, not trading it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed.
